text:
maria: Alert from the attestation pipeline — we're seeing a spike in model signature verification failures for artifacts signed by the 'mreg-signing-prod' key. Failing verifications started ~09:12 UTC. Suspect key exposure or misuse.

sre-bot: [ALERT] attestation-verify-failures > 100/min on mreg (service:mreg) — triggered at 2026-03-21T09:12:03Z.

maria: TL;DR: We need an emergency response: rotate the mreg signing key, block acceptance of signatures from the old key, and re-sign all active model artifacts. Also audit token usage for mreg service accounts.

jae: On it. I'll prepare a rotation plan and estimate time. Any known blast radius? Hosted + Dedicated pools + Private customers with on-prem cert sync.

maria: Blast radius: hosted inference + our model registry + any Dedicated clusters using the auto-sync signing cert (we push new attestations when models are promoted). Private on-prem customers may be unaffected if they didn't opt into auto-sync, but we need to notify them to rotate if they do.

alex: Quick ask: do we have a list of artifacts signed with that key? I can re-sign, but need the list and the recreate/redeploy window.

maria: Use this query in the registry DB:

```
SELECT artifact_id, version, signed_by, signing_ts
FROM model_signatures
WHERE signing_key = 'mreg-signing-prod'
AND signing_ts > '2025-01-01';
```

This will give current artifacts. Mark anything with 'deployed=true' as high priority for re-sign/redeploy.

jae: Rotation steps I'm going to run (draft):
1) create new keypair in KMS: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/mreg/cryptoKeys/mreg-signing-prod-v2
2) update mreg service to use new key in staging, smoke verify
3) set policy to reject signatures made by old key at the verifier layer (gateway + registry)
4) re-sign prioritized artifacts and publish new attestations
5) revoke old key access and schedule destroy after 7d quarantine

jae: ETA ~2.5 hours for staged rotation, 6-8 hours for full re-sign+deploy across Hosted + Dedicated.

nina: Legal/Compliance note: if any customers requested WORM artifact provenance we need to coordinate. Notify Compliance before revocation. I'll open a ticket.

ops-oncall: Ops checklist: run these detection queries to find service accounts that used the old key after 09:00 UTC:
```
gcloud logging read \"resource.labels.project_id=\\\"redwood-prod\\\" AND protoPayload.methodName:\\"SignBlob\\\" AND protoPayload.request.serviceAccountEmail:\\"mreg-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\\\" AND timestamp>\\\"2026-03-21T09:00:00Z\\\"\"
```

ops-oncall: If we see unexpected principals calling SignBlob, escalate to SecOps immediately.

maria: Temporary mitigation we'll apply now: verifier layer will start rejecting signatures from the old key (soft-fail mode for 10m to drain), then hard reject. This prevents replay of old attestation tokens.

alex: Re-signing plan: I'll take the top 50 deployed artifacts first. Re-signing will be done by a short job that pulls the model tar, re-computes digest, signs with new key, and pushes new attestation. I'll coordinate deploy windows with eng-runtime to avoid token mismatch during rollout.

jae: Patching verifier code in prod: will push canary to 10% traffic in 20 minutes, monitor verifier-errors, latency. Rollback plan ready.

maria: Communication: Security will send a short post to dedicated customers flagged as \"auto-sync enabled\" within 1 hour. We will offer a signed artifact list and rotation instructions for private on-prem teams.

nina: I created internal incident (INC-2026-03121) and compliance ticket COMPL-724. Adding legal and customer success to the incident.

ops-oncall: I ran the logging query — found 3 SignBlob calls from an external CI runner at 09:08 UTC. They used the mreg-sa credentials. Looks suspicious.

maria: Marking that as high priority. jae / ops-oncall - snapshot the CI runner, block the runner's network egress if possible, and rotate any CI tokens/keys. Add to incident notes.

jae: Blocking runner now and rotating mreg-sa keys. Also temporarily added a deny policy to verifier for signatures created after 2026-03-21T09:00:00Z by the old key (soft).

sre-bot: Deploy event: verifier-service v3.4.1 -> canary deployed to 10% at 2026-03-21T09:35:12Z.

maria: Update for re-sign timeline: alex, start re-sign job for top 50 now. jae, once canary looks good (30m), we escalate rollout. Ops, continue investigating CI runner.

alex: Starting re-sign jobs. Posting progress every 10 artifacts.

ops-oncall: CI runner was an automated workflow from partner-internal/infra-ci — partner access ticket raised. We've disabled that runner and rotated the associated token. No further SignBlob after 09:20 UTC.

nina: Drafting customer notice. Short, factual, and include mitigation steps + timeframe. Will ping CS to hold for 10m before sending.

maria: Good work team. I'll update execs and post a short incident summary after containment. Next actions: 1) finish rotation and re-sign 2) verify no new SignBlob use from unknown principals 3) customer notifications. Hold Qs here. :lock:

alex: 10/50 re-signed, 0 failures so far.

jae: Canary steady. No verifier errors. Proceeding with broader rollout to 50% in 15m.

maria: last note: after rotation completes, we will require a new attestation validation window in the SDKs — push a minor SDK release to accept mreg-signing-prod-v2. I'll loop in devex.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-03121 status -> CONTAINED (partial) at 2026-03-21T11:05:02Z.

maria: Closing thread here once all re-signs done and customer emails sent. Thanks everyone.

alex: re-signing complete for prioritized set. Pushing full re-sign backlog to background job.

ops-oncall: Audit logs show no additional anomalous SignBlob calls after rotation.

nina: Customer notice sent to affected Dedicated customers at 2026-03-21T12:02Z.

maria: Final: old key access revoked and scheduled destroy after 7-day quarantine. Incident moved to postmortem prep.
